name: Earthquake Checklist
description: A before, during and after earthquake checklist to secure your home and keep your family safe.

items.text: Anchor tall bookcases, cabinets and shelving to wall studs
Strap the water heater and major appliances to the wall
Install latches on cabinets to keep doors shut
Move heavy and breakable items to low, secure shelves
Keep beds away from windows and heavy hanging objects
Know how to shut off gas, water and electricity

sections.title: Before: Build Your Kit and Plan

items.text: Store one gallon of water per person per day for three days
Keep a three-day supply of non-perishable food and a can opener
Pack a first aid kit, medications and sturdy shoes by each bed
items.note: Broken glass after a quake makes shoes essential right where you sleep

items.text: Add flashlights, a radio, spare batteries and a whistle
Identify safe spots in every room away from windows
Set a family meeting place and an out-of-area contact
Practice Drop, Cover and Hold On with everyone in the home
Teach children how and when to call for help
Keep copies of key documents in a waterproof container
Plan how to reunite if family members are apart
Review the plan and refresh supplies twice a year

sections.title: During: Drop, Cover and Hold On

items.text: Drop to your hands and knees right where you are
Take cover under a sturdy table or against an interior wall
Hold on and protect your head and neck until shaking stops
Stay indoors and away from windows, mirrors and heavy furniture
If outdoors, move to an open area away from buildings and power lines
If driving, pull over safely and stay in the vehicle
Expect aftershocks and be ready to Drop, Cover and Hold On again
Check yourself and others for injuries and give first aid
Smell for gas; if you suspect a leak, shut it off and leave
Stay clear of downed power lines and broken glass
Inspect your home for damage before re-entering or staying
Listen to a battery radio for official information and updates

faq.q: What should I do during an earthquake?
faq.a: Drop, Cover and Hold On. Drop to your hands and knees, take cover under a sturdy table or against an interior wall, and hold on until the shaking stops. Stay where you are rather than running outside, where falling debris is most dangerous.

faq.q: How do I prepare my home for an earthquake?
faq.a: Fasten tall furniture, water heaters and shelving to wall studs, secure heavy items low, and use latches on cabinets. Know how to shut off gas and water, and identify safe spots in each room away from windows.

faq.q: How much water and food should I store for an earthquake?
faq.a: Keep at least one gallon of water per person per day and a three-day supply of non-perishable food, following Red Cross and Ready.gov guidance. Aim for two weeks at home, since utilities and water lines may be damaged.

faq.q: What are the biggest dangers after an earthquake?
faq.a: Aftershocks, gas leaks, downed power lines, broken glass and weakened structures. Check for hazards before moving around, expect aftershocks, and only re-enter damaged buildings once they are confirmed safe.
